input: Set up parental controls on all the kids' devices

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number and types of devices (phones, tablets, laptops, gaming consoles, smart TVs) determines the breadth of the plan and which control methods apply.
The ages of the children dramatically change what restrictions are appropriate — a toddler needs very different controls than a teenager.
The specific behaviors to restrict (screen time limits, content filtering, app purchases, social media, location tracking) define what features actually need to be configured.
Whether the family wants free built-in OS tools or is willing to pay for a dedicated third-party app (like Bark, Circle, or Qustodio) shapes the entire approach.
Knowing the operating systems (iOS, Android, Windows, macOS) determines which native parental control systems are available and how to access them.
Whether the user wants to manage everything from one central dashboard or configure each device individually affects which solution is recommended.
Understanding whether the goal is monitoring/alerting vs. hard blocking vs. scheduled limits clarifies how restrictive the setup should be and what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Set up parental controls on all kids' devices
gold.taskDescription: Configure parental controls across the children's devices to manage and restrict their digital activity appropriately.

questions.title: Which types of devices need parental controls set up?
questions.description: Identify all device categories involved — e.g., smartphones, tablets, laptops, gaming consoles, smart TVs — to determine which platforms and methods apply.

questions.title: How old are the children who will use these devices?
questions.description: The ages of the kids determine what restriction levels are appropriate, from strict content locks for young children to lighter monitoring for teenagers.

questions.title: What operating systems do the devices run on?
questions.description: Knowing whether devices are iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, or other platforms determines which built-in parental control tools are available.

questions.title: What specific behaviors are you most trying to control?
questions.description: Clarify the priority restrictions — such as screen time limits, content/app filtering, social media access, location tracking, or purchase controls — to focus the setup.

questions.title: Should the controls block content or just alert you to it?
questions.description: Determines whether the goal is hard restrictions (blocking), passive monitoring and alerts, or scheduled time limits — which defines how strictly controls need to be configured.

questions.title: Are you open to a paid app, or do you prefer free built-in tools?
questions.description: Decides whether to use free native OS features (Screen Time, Google Family Link) or invest in a paid third-party solution like Bark, Circle, or Qustodio for more control.

questions.title: Do you want one central dashboard to manage all devices?
questions.description: Establishes whether the parent wants a unified management interface across all devices or is comfortable configuring each device separately.
